group_assessment.counts_measured: PubMed esearch 2026-10-02: 'Freudenreich CH[au]' 68, 'Freudenreich CH[au] AND WWOX' 1 — this paper; 'Freudenreich CH[au] AND FRA16D' 5.
group_assessment.weighting: A primary group for REPEAT INSTABILITY AND FRAGILE SITES, not for WWOX. That is the correct weighting for what this paper measures: the breakage behaviour of a DNA sequence. It measures no WWOX protein and no WWOX function, and the gene name appears 9 times in 189,143 bytes.
group_assessment.note: Catherine Freudenreich, Tufts -- an established repeat-instability and fragile-site laboratory. The YAC breakage assay is the group's own, previously used for CAG/CTG repeats. The FRA16D clones were supplied by Richards and Finnis, the authors of the polymorphism survey this paper's key lead depends on, which is a shared-material dependency rather than an independent corroboration.

field_density.note: MEASURED EARNED NULL FOR DENSITY: 9 occurrences of 'WWOX' in 189,143 bytes, all of them naming the gene the fragile site spans or citing it as a tumour suppressor. This is a FRA16D paper, not a WWOX paper, and nothing in it measures WWOX.

multihop.enumeration_method: Reference anchors counted in the PMC HTML: 40. Not classified by gene-directedness.
multihop.note: ONE HOP QUEUED BY NAME AND IT IS THE DECIDING ONE: Finnis et al. 2005 holds both the Flex1 AT-allele distribution in the population and the position of Flex1 within the WWOX gene. This paper states neither, so nothing here can be placed against a named WWOX exon without it.

corpus_crossquery.query: Does the model's account of exon-scale deletion allele classes rest on any mechanism, and is that mechanism germline or somatic?
corpus_crossquery.finding: The model carries deletion allele classes phenotypically and names no breakage mechanism for them. This paper supplies a mechanism but for the wrong event class: every measurement here is somatic, mitotic, in yeast, and the authors' own prediction terminates in cancer-causing rearrangements. The transfer to germline deletion is unsupported and is written as such.

verbatim_locators.note: COVERAGE: whole author manuscript read, including every figure legend and the Experimental Procedures. NOT INSPECTED: the Supplemental Data (NIHMS28262-supplement-01.pdf), a separate file not fetched -- so the Southern-blot mapping of healing sites, Figure S1 (PFGE of the control YAC) and Figure S2 (yeast chromosome I flexibility) are carried only by the running text. WHAT THE PAPER DOES NOT LOCATE, AND IT MATTERS FOR THE ASSIGNMENT: the article never states which WWOX intron or exon Flex1 lies in. Figure 2B plots WWOX/FOR exons against the FlexStab trace, but the panel bytes were not inspected and no sentence in the body gives the position. Any statement placing Flex1 relative to a named WWOX exon would have to come from Finnis et al. 2005, which is not read.

entries.proposition: THE CORE RESULT AND ITS EXACT EVIDENCE CLASS: a yeast genetic assay, with a negative result for three of the four tested FRA16D sequences. The specificity is what makes it a real finding rather than 'AT-rich DNA breaks'.
entries.snippet: We have developed an assay to study human common fragile site FRA16D in yeast and used it to test whether regions of high flexibility increase chromosome breakage in a quantitative manner. We report that a short ~500 bp AT rich region that spans the peak of highest flexibility and contains a polymorphic perfect AT repeat increases chromosome fragility, whereas three other tested sequences within FRA16D do not.

entries.proposition: THE MECHANISM, MEASURED: fork stalling on 2-D gels, scaling with the length of the AT repeat. This is the part that could in principle transfer to any organism's replication.
entries.snippet: we have demonstrated that the Flex1 region stalls replication fork progression in a manner dependent on the length of a variable perfect AT repeat predicted to form a cruciform structure

entries.proposition: THE GERMLINE-RELEVANT HOOK, AND THE ONE GENUINELY NEW LEAD THIS PAPER OFFERS THE DISEASE MODEL: the fragility determinant is a COMMON HUMAN POLYMORPHISM with an 11-88 repeat range, so it is a candidate genomic covariate that is genotypable from blood.
entries.snippet: highly polymorphic in the population (97% heterozygosity) with alleles varying between 11–88 AT repeats, and alleles of 34 repeats or greater are quite common.
entries.anchor: Discussion, 'A Model for the Mechanism behind the Chromosome Breaks and Rearrangements Found at Common Fragile Sites', citing Finnis et al. 2005

entries.proposition: THE AUTHORS' OWN PREDICTION, AND NOTE ITS ENDPOINT: cancer-causing rearrangements. The paper's entire frame is somatic and oncological; it predicts nothing about germline or developmental disease.
entries.snippet: The fact that longer Flex1 AT alleles caused a significantly stronger replication barrier predicts that human alleles with longer AT length at the Flex1 locus could predispose to cancer-causing rearrangements in the FRA16D region.
entries.anchor: Discussion, 'The Consequences of Fork Stalling in the FRA16D Flex1 Region', final sentence

entries.proposition: AND THE AUTHORS RECORD THAT THE HUMAN ASSOCIATION IS ABSENT AND THEIR OWN EFFECT IS SUBTLE. This is the sentence that stops the lead from being written as anything stronger than a hypothesis.
entries.snippet: Although a relationship between AT length and fragility could not be documented in the Finnis et al. study, a comparison of fragility rates of the different alleles in our assay suggests that the effect may be subtle.
entries.anchor: Discussion, same subsection, sentence following the polymorphism sentence

entries.proposition: The Figure 2 legend states that the panel carries the WWOX/FOR exon track beneath the FRA16D flexibility trace, and that the assayed regions are drawn on the same axis. The gene-relative position of Flex1 is therefore published in the figure, not in the running text.
entries.snippet: Below it, the exons of the WWOX/FOR gene are represented by grey boxes.

entries.proposition: Figure 2B inspected: the exon track beneath the FlexStab trace carries two labelled grey boxes, 'WWOX exon 8' at the left end of the plotted FRA16D interval and 'WWOX exon 9' at the right end, and the black box marked Flex1 sits between them, as do the black boxes marked Flex4, Control and Flex5-p. The figure therefore places all four assayed regions, Flex1 included, between WWOX exons 8 and 9 (i.e. in intron 8), which the running text never states.
entries.snippet: [figure attestation - pixels cannot be quote-matched] Figure 2 panel B: FlexStab score plotted against bases 0-300000 with a 'FRA16D' span bar; beneath it a track whose left and right grey boxes are labelled 'WWOX exon 8' and 'WWOX exon 9', with black boxes labelled Flex4, Control, Flex1 and Flex5-p in between, Flex1 near the middle under flexibility peak 2.
